sources.entry: OffPDF - An offline PDF toolkit with 23 tools for editing, converting, organizing, OCR, and more.

summary.one_liner: OffPDF is a free, MIT-licensed desktop toolbox with 23 PDF tools that process files locally with engines like qpdf, Poppler, Tesseract, and LibreOffice, without uploads or accounts.
summary.what_it_does: OffPDF bundles 23 PDF tools grouped into Organize (merge, split, organize pages, page numbers, watermark, crop, stamp/sign, edit, poster tiling, N-up/booklet, compare, remove blank pages), Convert (Office/HTML to PDF, PDF to Office, PDF to images, OCR, PDF/A, PDF to text), and Optimize & secure (compress, protect, unlock, repair, edit metadata). The Edit PDF workspace adds text, images, shapes, links, freehand drawing, and annotations, and can fill existing AcroForm fields and flatten forms or annotations. Editing an existing text line is supported only in limited cases where the change can be verified; the original file is never overwritten. Results are written to new files. The desktop app is built with Tauri (Rust backend, React and TypeScript frontend), and the README says it has no telemetry and auto-update is disabled. Packaged builds register as an Open With handler for PDFs, images, and Office files.
use_cases: merge or split PDF files offline
convert Office documents to PDF privately
make scanned PDFs searchable with OCR
compress or repair a PDF without uploading it
fill in and flatten PDF forms
add watermarks, page numbers, or signatures to PDFs
how_to_run: brew install qpdf poppler tesseract (macOS; optional engines)
brew install --cask libreoffice (macOS; optional, for Office and PDF/A tools)
sudo apt install qpdf poppler-utils tesseract-ocr libreoffice (Debian/Ubuntu)
npm run tauri:build (create a desktop bundle)
notable: Runs entirely offline with no uploads, accounts, or telemetry; original files are never overwritten
23 tools in one app covering organize, convert, OCR, compress, protect, and repair
Edit PDF can change existing text in the document's own font when the change can be verified
Uses existing local engines (qpdf, Poppler, Tesseract, LibreOffice) rather than a cloud service
Registers as an Open With handler in packaged builds without becoming the default PDF app
caveats: Windows build is currently unsigned; no published package yet for Intel Mac or Linux (build from source)
XFA forms are not supported, and only the first PDF's AcroForm can be filled when several are combined
Editing existing text does not reflow paragraphs, add fonts, or handle rotated, scanned, signed, or encrypted PDFs; many tools need optional engines installed
